style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings; 'the LORD' for YHWH; deity pronouns capitalized.
chapterNote: The coronation psalm, and with Psalm 1 the double gateway into the whole Psalter: Psalm 1 sets the two ways before one man; Psalm 2 sets the one King before all nations. Four voices speak in turn. The nations rage and their kings convene, plotting to snap the cords of the LORD and His Anointed -- His Mashiach, His Messiah. Heaven answers first with laughter, the only time derision is holy: He who sits enthroned is not pacing. Then the Father's decree, the psalm's center: 'You are My Son; today I have begotten You' -- the verse the New Testament quotes at Jesus' baptism, His transfiguration, and His resurrection (Acts 13:33; Hebrews 1:5), with the nations promised Him for an inheritance to the ends of the earth. Finally wisdom addresses the rebels themselves: be wise, you kings; serve the LORD with fear, rejoice with trembling, kiss the Son -- homage before He is angry, for His wrath kindles in a moment. And the psalm that began with rage ends where Psalm 1 began, with blessedness: oh the happiness of all who take refuge in Him. The rebels' choice was never revolt or freedom; it was ruin or refuge.

1.text: Why do the nations rage in an uproar, and the peoples keep muttering an empty thing?
1.amp: Why do the heathen [goy -- the nations] rage ['tumultuously assemble', ragash, the KJV margin], and the people [leom] imagine ['meditate', hagah, the KJV margin -- mutter, growl over] a vain thing [riq -- an empty thing]?
1.notes: ragash (H7283) is the roar of a mob assembling, and hagah (H1897) is Psalm 1:2's meditation-verb turned upside down: the blessed man mutters torah day and night, the leom (H3816) mutter riq (H7385), emptiness. Same faculty, opposite feed. The apostles prayed this verse over the crucifixion coalition (cf. Acts 4:25-26).

2.text: The kings of the earth take their stand, and the rulers convene as one, against the LORD and against His Anointed:
2.amp: The kings [melek] of the earth [eretz] set [yatsab -- station] themselves, and the rulers [razan] take counsel [yasad -- found their session] together [yachad], against the LORD [YHWH], and against His anointed [mashiach -- His Messiah], saying,
2.notes: yatsab (H3320) is military posture, and yasad (H3245), the founding-verb: rebellion organized as an institution. The target is a pair that cannot be split -- YHWH and His mashiach (H4899): the word is Messiah, and in Greek dress, Christ. Every revolt against the Son is a revolt against the Father (cf. John 5:23).

3.text: 'Let us tear their bonds apart and throw their cords off of us!'
3.amp: 'Let us break [nathaq -- tear apart] their bands [moserah -- bonds, restraints] asunder, and cast away [shalak] their cords [avoth -- braided ropes] from us.'
3.notes: The rebels' one recorded sentence: God's rule pictured as moserot (H4147) and avoth (H5688), harness and rope -- law as bondage. The tragedy is the misreading: the 'cords' they tear at are the very bindings of love and blessing (cf. Hosea 11:4); freedom from God is the one slavery with no emancipation.

4.text: He who sits enthroned in the heavens laughs; the Lord holds them in derision.
4.amp: He that sits [yashab -- sits enthroned] in the heavens [shamayim] shall laugh [sachaq]: the Lord [Adonai] shall have them in derision [laag -- mock them].
4.notes: Heaven's first response to the summit of the kings is neither alarm nor argument: sachaq (H7832), laughter. yashab (H3427) is the enthroned sitting -- the coup has not moved Him an inch off His seat. The only holy derision in Scripture is omnipotence regarding a rebellion of clay.

5.text: Then He speaks to them in His anger, and in His burning fury He throws them into terror:
5.amp: Then shall He speak [dabar] unto them in His wrath [aph], and vex ['trouble', bahal, the KJV margin -- terrify] them in His sore displeasure [charon -- burning anger].
5.notes: The laughter gives way to the word: dabar (H1696) -- He need only speak. bahal (H926) is the panic-verb, and charon (H2740) anger at full burn. What He says, verse 6 gives: not a battle plan but an announcement of something already done.

6.text: 'But I -- I have installed My King on Zion, the mountain of My holiness.'
6.amp: 'Yet have I set ['anointed', nasak, the KJV margin -- poured out, installed] My king [melek] upon My holy [qodesh] hill [har] of Zion ['upon Zion, the hill of My holiness', Tsiyyon, the KJV margin].'
6.notes: nasak (H5258) is to pour -- installation by anointing oil, kingship poured on. The rebellion is answered in the perfect tense: the King is already seated on Tsiyyon (H6726) while the committee is still drafting resolutions. History's outcome was settled before its argument began.

7.text: I will recount the decree: the LORD said to Me, 'You are My Son; this day I have begotten You.
7.amp: I will declare [saphar -- recount] the decree [choq]: the LORD [YHWH] has said [amar] unto Me, 'You are My Son [ben]; this day [yom] have I begotten [yalad] You.'
7.notes: The King Himself now speaks, reading out the choq (H2706), the standing decree of His sonship. The New Testament unseals the verse three ways: at the baptism and transfiguration ('This is My beloved Son'), and Paul preaches 'this day' as the resurrection -- the Son begotten from the dead into enthroned glory (cf. Acts 13:33; Hebrews 1:5; 5:5; Romans 1:4).

8.text: Ask it of Me, and I will give the nations as Your inheritance, and the far ends of the earth as Your possession.
8.amp: Ask [shaal] of Me, and I shall give [natan] You the heathen [goy -- the nations] for Your inheritance [nachalah], and the uttermost parts [ephes] of the earth [eretz] for Your possession [achuzzah].
8.notes: The Father's standing offer to the Son: the raging goyim of verse 1 handed over as nachalah (H5159), family inheritance -- the rebels themselves the estate. ephes eretz (H657), the ends of the earth: the Great Commission is this verse being collected (cf. Matthew 28:18-19; Revelation 11:15).

9.text: You will break them with a rod of iron; You will shatter them like a potter's jar.'
9.amp: 'You shall break [raa] them with a rod [shebet -- the scepter] of iron [barzel]; You shall dash them in pieces [naphats -- shatter] like a potter's [yatsar] vessel [keli].'
9.notes: The shebet barzel (H7626, H1270), the iron scepter: rule that rebellion cannot bend. The yatsar-vessel (H3335) image cuts deep -- the nations are the Potter's own clay (cf. Psalm 139's forming-verb), and clay that wars on its maker meets the floor. Revelation gives this verse to the conquering Christ and to His overcomers (cf. Revelation 2:26-27; 19:15).

10.text: Now therefore, you kings, act wisely; take the correction, you judges of the earth.
10.amp: Be wise [sakal] now therefore, O ye kings [melek]: be instructed [yasar -- take discipline, be corrected], ye judges [shaphat] of the earth [eretz].
10.notes: The psalm turns pastoral toward the very rebels it has sentenced: sakal (H7919), the applied-wisdom verb, and yasar (H3256), to receive correction -- the door of repentance held open for kings mid-conspiracy. Judgment announced is still mercy offered.

11.text: Serve the LORD with reverent fear, and rejoice with trembling in your joy.
11.amp: Serve [avad] the LORD [YHWH] with fear [yirah], and rejoice [gil -- exult] with trembling [raad -- shuddering awe].
11.notes: The startling pair: gil (H1523), spinning joy, wedded to raad (H7461), the shudder. Right worship holds both -- joy without trembling grows flippant, trembling without joy grows servile. avad (H5647): the rebels' new employment, service in place of sedition.

12.text: Kiss the Son, lest He be angry and you perish in the way, for His wrath can blaze up in a moment. Oh the blessedness of all who take refuge in Him!
12.amp: Kiss [nashaq] the Son [bar], lest He be angry [anaph], and ye perish [abad] from the way [derek], when His wrath [aph] is kindled [baar] but a little [meat]. Blessed [esher] are all they that put their trust [chasah -- take refuge] in Him.
12.notes: nashaq (H5401), the kiss of homage a vassal gave his king: allegiance pressed to the Son's feet before the aph (H639) ignites -- baar (H1197), the kindling-verb, needs only meat, a little. And the last line swings the gate wide: esher (H835), the blessedness that opened Psalm 1, now pronounced over ALL who chasah (H2620) in Him -- kings and commoners alike, safe not from the Son but IN Him.
